description: A curator and conservator must decide which objects need attention first based on fragility, current condition, exhibit schedule, research value, and the consequences of deferring treatment.

user_profile.persona: 45-year-old collections leader managing more needs than conservation capacity
user_profile.context: Nothing is in immediate disaster mode, but postponing the wrong items could create avoidable damage later
user_profile.communication_style: Prioritization-oriented and evidence-based, wants decisions tied to object-specific risk

fact_sheet.fact: The collections management software is named 'CollectioDB' and is accessible internally at the URL https://ama.collectiodb.internal.
The Head Conservator, Lena Petrova, can be reached at office phone extension 721 or via email at l.petrova@aethelburgmuseum.org.
Dr. Aris Thorne, the Collections Leader, reviews object condition reports at his workstation, C-04, in the Curatorial Office.
The conservation lab currently has a documented backlog of 240 work-hours as of July 1, 2024.
The estimated conservation time required to stabilize the 'Scribe's Palette of Amenhotep' (AMA-EGY-0112) is 80 hours.
Consolidating the crack on the 'Etruscan Terracotta Sarcophagus Lid' requires a specific acrylic resin, Paraloid B-72, which has a 3-week delivery lead time.
The museum's fiscal year 2024 conservation budget has $8,500 remaining for specialized materials and external consultations.
The 'Scribe's Palette of Amenhotep' (AMA-EGY-0112), made of ivory, is rated at Condition Score 4/5 (5=Critical) due to observed micro-cracks.
The 'Etruscan Terracotta Sarcophagus Lid' (AMA-ETR-0089) has a stable 12cm hairline crack near its base, documented on May 20, 2024.
The 'Roman Glass Amphora' (AMA-ROM-0351) is exhibiting early-stage crizzling, a form of glass disease.
'The Mariner's Astrolabe' (AMA-REN-0045) is structurally stable (Condition Score: 2/5), but heavy surface tarnish obscures its scientific engravings.
The 'Qing Dynasty Silk Robe' (AMA-QIN-0210) has a cumulative light exposure of 45,000 lux hours, approaching its annual limit of 50,000 lux hours.
The environmental monitor in Storage Bay 4C, housing the 'Roman Glass Amphora', registered a peak relative humidity of 65% on June 15, 2024, exceeding the recommended 45% RH.
The last condition report for the 'Scribe's Palette of Amenhotep' (AMA-EGY-0112) was filed by Lena Petrova on June 1, 2024.
The 'Scribe's Palette of Amenhotep' (AMA-EGY-0112) is a confirmed highlight object for the 'Echoes of the Nile' exhibition, opening October 15, 2024.
All objects for the 'Echoes of the Nile' exhibition must be moved to the pre-exhibit staging area by September 1, 2024.
'The Mariner's Astrolabe' (AMA-REN-0045) is scheduled for the 'Navigating the Renaissance' exhibition in the third quarter of 2025.
The 'Qing Dynasty Silk Robe' (AMA-QIN-0210) is not scheduled for public display within the next 24 months.
Dr. Evelyn Reed from Northwood University has formally requested access to the 'Etruscan Terracotta Sarcophagus Lid' for non-destructive XRF analysis in November 2024.
Dr. Reed's research access is contingent on the object being stable enough for transport from storage to the on-site imaging lab.
A pending publication by Dr. Alistair Finch requires new high-resolution photographs of 'The Mariner's Astrolabe' after its tarnish is removed.
Deferring treatment on the 'Roman Glass Amphora' (AMA-ROM-0351) carries a high risk of irreversible surface weeping if humidity is not stabilized within the next 3 months.
The consequence of not stabilizing the 'Scribe's Palette of Amenhotep' (AMA-EGY-0112) is a high probability of crack propagation and material loss during transport for exhibition.
Postponing the cleaning of 'The Mariner's Astrolabe' (AMA-REN-0045) has a low risk of structural damage but will delay Dr. Finch's research publication by an estimated six months.
The fragility of the 'Qing Dynasty Silk Robe' (AMA-QIN-0210) is primarily linked to light exposure and fiber degradation, not immediate handling risks.
The weekly conservation prioritization meeting between Dr. Aris Thorne and Lena Petrova occurs every Tuesday at 10:00 AM in the Harrison Conference Room.
The estimated time to clean and apply a protective coating to 'The Mariner's Astrolabe' (AMA-REN-0045) is 25 hours.
